fix.note: Often used like 'at least': 최소 한 시간.

ex.en: It takes at least an hour to the airport.
The minimum order is 10,000 won.

ex.s: 하루에 물을 최소 일 리터는 마셔요.
ex.en: I drink at least a liter of water a day.
I have a presentation at tomorrow's meeting.
I stayed up all night preparing my presentation.
When are the exam results announced?

fix.note: Emphatic; in casual speech -만 alone is more common.

ex.en: Dad thinks only of his family.
This shop takes cash only.
I drink nothing but coffee.
I work out at least three times a week.
You should have at least called.
It takes at least thirty minutes to get there.

fix.note: 축제 is the more general Korean word.

ex.en: I'm going to a music festival this weekend.
The festival tickets sold out.
I met my friend at last year's festival.
The bride was really beautiful.
Here come the bride and groom!
I said hello to the priest at the Catholic church.

ex.s: 그 영화 보고 웃음이 안 멈췄어요.
ex.en: I couldn't stop laughing at that movie.
The baby's laugh is so cute.
I held in a laugh during the meeting.
The parking lot is on B2.
There's a food court in the basement.
I live in a basement unit, so it's damp.
I welcomed my family at the airport.
I rang in the New Year with friends.

ex.s: 결혼 십 주년을 맞이해서 여행 가요.
ex.en: We're taking a trip to mark our 10th anniversary.

notes: Fixes: non-standard 샜어요→새웠어요, 웃음소리 spacing, tense mismatch (했어야죠), awkward word order, 축제 wrongly called native Korean, 오직 note, 성당≠cathedral.
